theorem_title: Weighted-ideal membership of the formal logarithm tail
natural_language_statement: Let m be a natural number, let v : Fin (m + 1) → ℚ be nonnegative in every coordinate, and let T and H satisfy H ≤ T · v(0). Then the series logTail(T), embedded into coordinate 0 of the multivariate power-series ring, belongs to the rational weighted ideal determined by v and H. Here logTail(T) is the formal power-series logarithm log(X) minus its truncation below degree T; the statement is algebraic and makes no analytic convergence claim.
explanation: The hypothesis H ≤ T · v(0) places every potentially nonzero coefficient of the logarithm tail beyond the weighted-degree cutoff H along the distinguished coordinate 0. Coefficients below T vanish by the definition of logTail, while any exponent supported only at coordinate 0 and below the weighted cutoff would force its degree to be at least T, contradicting the weight bound. The result is a formal-series membership statement for the campaign's rational weighted ideal, not an analytic estimate.
